rationale: 11 patch findings span one critical frontend regression (registrations tab always empty after API shape change), four backend 404-correctness gaps (getRegistrations, getConferenceSessions, and the two deleteRegistration error-status cases), one NPE on missing status field in updateConference, one catch-all handler that converts Spring MVC framework exceptions to 500, one inconsistent empty 400 body on date-range validation, and three test coverage gaps for changed behaviour; brief written to code-review-brief.md. 3 candidates dismissed as noise (FQN style on controller imports, redundant 500-message test, paginated list endpoint already includes a `data` key); no findings deferred.

findings.title: Date-range validation returns 400 with empty body
findings.problem: When `from` is after `to`, the handler calls `ResponseEntity.badRequest().<Map<String, Object>>build()`, producing a 400 response with no body.
findings.impact: Clients relying on the ErrorResponse contract receive a bodyless 400; error-handling middleware that parses `$.status` or `$.message` fails silently. This is the only endpoint in the change that violates the structured-error rule it establishes.
findings.recommendation: Replace `.build()` with `.body(new ErrorResponse(400, "Bad Request", "\"from\" must not be after \"to\""))` to emit a structured error body consistent with all other error paths.

findings.title: Catch-all converts Spring MVC framework exceptions to 500
findings.problem: `GlobalExceptionHandler` does not extend `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler`. `ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver` (ORDER 1) intercepts Spring MVC's own exceptions — `HttpMessageNotReadableException` (malformed JSON), `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` (bad path variable type), `NoHandlerFoundException` — before `DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver` (ORDER 3) can map them to 400/404. All fall through to `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)` and return 500.
findings.impact: Clients sending malformed JSON or a non-numeric path variable receive a 500 instead of 400/404. The established ErrorResponse contract is violated for the most common client mistakes; automated clients parsing the status field will interpret user errors as server failures.
findings.recommendation: Extend `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler` and override `handleHttpMessageNotReadable` and `handleMethodArgumentTypeMismatch` (or add a dedicated `@ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException.class)`) to return structured `ErrorResponse` bodies at the correct status codes.

findings.title: Null status field causes NullPointerException in updateConference
findings.problem: `updateConference` calls `conf.getStatus().toUpperCase()` unconditionally. A PUT request body that omits `status` causes a NullPointerException caught by the `Exception.class` handler, which returns 500.
findings.impact: Any PUT request without the `status` field returns an opaque 500 instead of a meaningful error. Partial-update requests that are otherwise valid always fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a null guard: `if (conf.getStatus() != null) existing.setStatus(conf.getStatus().toUpperCase());` — or explicitly reject a null status with a 400 Bad Request if the field is required.

findings.title: getConferenceSessions returns 200 with empty page for missing conference
findings.problem: `getConferenceSessions` calls `sessionRepository.findPageByConferenceId(id, pageable)` with no prior conference-existence check. A non-existent conference ID returns an empty `{"data":[]}` page with HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Clients cannot distinguish a valid conference with no sessions from a conference that does not exist. The 404 contract established for other `ConferenceService` methods in this change is absent here.
findings.recommendation: Add `conferenceRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow(() -> new ResourceNotFoundException("Conference not found"));` before the session query, mirroring the pattern used in `createSession`.

findings.title: getRegistrations returns 200 with empty list for missing conference
findings.problem: `getRegistrations` at line 43-44 calls `registrationRepository.findByConferenceId(conferenceId)` directly with no conference-existence check. A non-existent conference ID returns an empty list with HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Clients cannot distinguish a real empty registration list from a non-existent conference. This is the same class of defect as CR-004 and was explicitly left unaddressed in the diff while all sibling methods in the service were updated.
findings.recommendation: Add `conferenceRepository.findById(conferenceId).orElseThrow(() -> new ResourceNotFoundException("Conference not found"));` before the repository call.

findings.title: deleteRegistration returns misleading 400 instead of 404 for absent registration
findings.problem: `existsByIdAndConferenceId` returns false for two distinct cases: the registration does not exist at all, and the registration exists but belongs to a different conference. Both throw `RegistrationMismatchException` → 400 with message "Registration does not belong to this conference".
findings.impact: A completely absent registration ID returns a misleading 400 "does not belong" message instead of a correct 404, violating the HTTP semantics this change was intended to establish.
findings.recommendation: Add a prior existence check: `if (!registrationRepository.existsById(registrationId)) throw new ResourceNotFoundException("Registration not found");` before the conference-membership check.

findings.title: RegistrationService exception contract not tested at service level
findings.problem: `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.mismatch_shouldReturn400WithErrorShape` exercises the handler by throwing `RegistrationMismatchException` directly from a stub controller that bypasses `RegistrationService`. A reversion of `deleteRegistration` to throwing `IllegalArgumentException` would not be caught by any test; the test suite would still pass.
findings.impact: The service-to-handler contract for registration mismatch errors has no regression protection at the service layer. No `RegistrationServiceTest` exists in the project.
findings.recommendation: Add a `RegistrationServiceTest` with at least: `assertThrows(RegistrationMismatchException.class, () -> registrationService.deleteRegistration(conferenceId, nonMatchingId))`.

findings.title: TestController double-registered via @WebMvcTest and @Import
findings.problem: `@WebMvcTest(controllers = TestController.class)` registers `TestController`; `@Import({GlobalExceptionHandler.class, TestController.class})` imports it again. With Spring Boot's default `spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding=false`, this can cause a `BeanDefinitionOverrideException` at test startup. Confirmed present in source; whether it fails in practice is uncertain across Spring Boot 2.7.x patch versions.
findings.impact: The test class may fail to start on some configurations, silently disabling all exception-handler test coverage.
findings.recommendation: Remove `TestController.class` from the `@Import` list, keeping only `@Import({GlobalExceptionHandler.class})`.

findings.title: No ResourceNotFoundException tests for ConferenceService not-found paths
findings.problem: This change adds `orElseThrow(() -> new ResourceNotFoundException(...))` to `getConference`, `updateConference`, and `createSession` in `ConferenceService`. `ConferenceServiceTest` adds no not-found test for any of them, while `SessionServiceTest` introduces the pattern for `getSession`.
findings.impact: The 404 contract for all three conference service operations is completely untested. A regression (e.g., reverting any orElseThrow to `.get()`) would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add `@Test` methods asserting `assertThrows(ResourceNotFoundException.class, ...)` for `getConference(99L)`, `updateConference(99L, ...)`, and `createSession(99L, ...)` in `ConferenceServiceTest`.

findings.title: updateSession not-found path has no test
findings.problem: `SessionService.updateSession` was changed in this diff to use `.orElseThrow(() -> new ResourceNotFoundException("Session not found"))`. `SessionServiceTest` adds `getSession_notFound_shouldThrowResourceNotFoundException` but has no counterpart for `updateSession`.
findings.impact: The not-found contract for `updateSession` (PUT /api/sessions/{id}) is untested; a reversion of that orElseThrow would not be detected.
findings.recommendation: Add `updateSession_notFound_shouldThrowResourceNotFoundException` to `SessionServiceTest`, mirroring the existing `getSession_notFound` pattern.

findings.title: Registrations tab always empty after API response shape change
findings.problem: `RegistrationController.getRegistrations` was changed to return `{"data": [...]}` instead of a bare JSON array. `frontend/src/api.js:getConferenceRegistrations` returns `response.json()` directly, which is now the envelope object. `ConferenceDetailPage.jsx:66` calls `setRegistrations(Array.isArray(data) ? data : [])` — `Array.isArray({data:[...]})` is always false, so every successful response sets the registrations list to `[]`.
findings.impact: The registrations tab always renders "No registrations yet" after this change regardless of real data. Existing registrations are invisible in the UI. This is a live runtime regression introduced by the API contract change without a corresponding frontend update.
findings.recommendation: Update `ConferenceDetailPage.jsx:66` to `setRegistrations(Array.isArray(data.data) ? data.data : [])`. Additionally update `api.js:getConferenceRegistrations` to unwrap the envelope consistently: `const res = await response.json(); return res.data ?? res;`.
